newsitem.title: GERMANY: Higher U.S. oilseed crops seen relieving tightness.
newsitem.headline: Higher U.S. oilseed crops seen relieving tightness.

text.p: Latest forecasts for bigger U.S. oilseeds crops should help ease a global tightness in the 1996/97 season, but consumers may still need to draw down stocks to meet demand, independent newsletter Oil World said.
The USDA November 13 report revised output of all U.S. oilseeds to 74.8 million tonnes, 1.7 million up from the October estimate and 6.1 million tonnes above last year, it noted.
Pegging U.S. soybean output alone at 65.39 million tonnes (versus 59.24 million 95/96), Oil World estimated the 96/97 U.S. soybean crush at 38 million tonnes (37.26 previously).
It put 96/97 U.S. bean exports at 24 million tonnes (23.26) last season and end-season stocks at 5.3 million (4.99).
Oil World put global supplies of 10 key oilseeds at 288.3 million tonnes, three million tonnes down from 95/96.
Output of oilseeds was expected sharply lower in China, the former USSR, Canada, eastern Europe, the EU and Pakistan.
It stressed importers were dependent on ample crops in Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay to offset the shortfalls even if the U.S. stepped up its exports.
Oil World put oilseeds output in the three countries at 49.3 million tonnes, up 2.6 million from last year, but added 50 million tonnes may be possible amid exceptional weather.
